full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land. Her case in short is that the suit land belonged to Moulovi Abdul Majid, who transferred the same to his son Md. Wasek by a deed dated 10th August, 1956. Said Wasek thereupon gifted the said land in favour of his mother Most. Amina Khatun by a deed of heba-bil-ewaj dated 11th June, 1958. Amina Khatun in turn gifted 7 kathas of land to her son Md. Wasek by a registered deed of gift dated 2nd February, 1959 and by another deed of the same date gifted the remaining 7 kathas of land to her another son Abdul Motalib Said Motalib died leaving three sons and one daughter, who inherited the said land and thereafter they by a deed dated 5th November, 1992 transferred the suit land in favour of the plaintiff and delivered possession. Plaintiff was in possession the suit land through her caretaker and ultimately she was dispossessed on 4th May, 2006 which constituted the cause of action of the suit. 

 7. The plaintiff claimed declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land. In order to prove a suit of the nature, the plaintiff must prove her possession first and then her dispossession by the defendants within the statutory period of limitation. The High Court Division as well as the trial Court came to a definite finding that Abdul Motalib never got possession in pursuance of deed of gift dated 2nd February, 1959. In the absence of proof of Motalib's possession, even if it is assumed that Amina Khatun gifted the suit land in favour of Abdul Motalib it was not acted upon. Abdul Motalib never got possession of the suit land. Learned counsel for the petitioner finds it difficult to assail the concurrent findings of the defendants' possession in the suit land. Therefore, we find no merit in the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner.
